```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(limma)       # camera: competitive gene set test
library(fgsea)       # pre-ranked gene set enrichment analysis
library(tidyverse)   # loaded after Bioconductor packages, so dplyr verbs are not masked
library(DT)          # interactive downloadable tables
library(knitr)       # kable for simple inline tables
```

# From Module 2

Module 2 found thousands of genes changed between the tumors and the normal kidneys of the same children. A list that long cannot be read gene by gene. This module asks a different question: **do the genes of a known biological program move together?**

**Plan:** gene sets → two kinds of test → `camera` (limma) → GSEA (`fgsea`) → do the methods agree? → GO terms with redundancy collapsed.

```{r load-data, echo=TRUE}
# Same matrix, sample sheet and paired design as Module 2.
tumor_tpm   <- read_csv("data/TARGET_WT_gene_expression_tpm.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
control_tpm <- read_csv("data/TARGET_WT_control_gene_expression_tpm.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tumor_metadata   <- read_csv("data/sample_metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
control_metadata <- read_csv("data/TARGET_WT_control_clinical_raw.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

tpm <- as.matrix(bind_cols(tumor_tpm[, -1], control_tpm[, -1]))
rownames(tpm) <- tumor_tpm$gene_name
samples <- bind_rows(
  tumor_metadata %>% transmute(sample_id = case_submitter_id, patient = case_submitter_id, condition = "Tumor"),
  control_metadata %>% transmute(sample_id = sample_submitter_id, patient = case_submitter_id, condition = "Normal")
) %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Normal", "Tumor")), patient = factor(patient))
samples <- samples[match(colnames(tpm), samples$sample_id), ]
stopifnot(identical(samples$sample_id, colnames(tpm)))

log_expr <- log2(tpm[rowSums(tpm >= 1) >= min(table(samples$condition)), ] + 1)
design_paired <- model.matrix(~ patient + condition, data = samples)

# Module 2's paired results.
limma_results <- read_csv("results/limma_tumor_vs_normal_paired.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Part 1 — Gene Sets

A **gene set** is a list of genes sharing a function. We use two collections from **MSigDB**, saved in `data/` by `data-prep/build_gene_sets.R`:

- **Hallmark** (50 sets): compact, curated, non-redundant summaries of well-defined biological states, e.g. `HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS` (cell-cycle genes switched on by E2F) or `HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION`. The best starting point.
- **GO Biological Process** (thousands of sets): detailed and hierarchical, but highly redundant.

```{r gene-sets, echo=TRUE}
hallmark <- gmtPathways("data/msigdb_hallmark.gmt")
go_bp    <- gmtPathways("data/msigdb_go_bp.gmt")

min_size <- 15
max_size <- 500

pretty_name <- function(x) str_replace_all(str_remove(x, "^(HALLMARK|GOBP)_"), "_", " ")
```

# Part 2 — Two Questions You Can Ask of a Gene Set

| | **Competitive** test | **Self-contained** test |
|---|---|---|
| question | are the set's genes *more* changed than the other genes? | are the set's genes changed *at all*? |
| examples | `camera`, GSEA, ORA | `roast`, `fry` (limma) |
| when tumor vs normal changes thousands of genes | still informative | almost every set is "significant" |

We use **competitive** tests: they tell us which programs stand out *relative to* the general change.

<div class="alert-info">
**The hidden problem: genes are correlated.** Genes of one pathway tend to go up and down together across samples. Many gene set tests treat them as independent, which makes them far too confident (p-values much too small). **camera** (*Correlation Adjusted MEan RAnk*) estimates the average correlation between the genes of each set and corrects the test for it. It is limma's recommended competitive test and works directly on the expression matrix and the design, here the paired one.
</div>

# Part 3 — camera

```{r camera, echo=TRUE}
hallmark_index <- ids2indices(hallmark, rownames(log_expr))

# contrast = the coefficient to test, by name: the tumor effect of the paired design.
camera_results <- camera(log_expr, index = hallmark_index, design = design_paired, contrast = "conditionTumor") %>%
  rownames_to_column("pathway") %>%
  as_tibble()
```

```{r table-camera-summary}
kable(tibble(sets_tested = nrow(camera_results),
             `FDR < 0.05, up in tumor` = sum(camera_results$FDR < 0.05 & camera_results$Direction == "Up"),
             `FDR < 0.05, down in tumor` = sum(camera_results$FDR < 0.05 & camera_results$Direction == "Down")),
      caption = "camera on the 50 Hallmark sets.")
```

```{r plot-camera, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
camera_results %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.05) %>%
  slice_min(FDR, n = 25, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(score = -log10(FDR) * if_else(Direction == "Up", 1, -1),
         label = fct_reorder(pretty_name(pathway), score)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score, y = label, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Up = "#e74c3c", Down = "#2980b9"), labels = c(Up = "Up in tumor", Down = "Down in tumor")) +
  labs(x = "signed -log10(FDR)  (right: up in tumor, left: down)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "camera: the 25 most significant Hallmark sets") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Part 4 — GSEA with fgsea

**GSEA** ranks all genes from most up to most down and asks whether a set's genes concentrate at one end of the list. We rank by the **moderated t-statistic** of Module 2 (it combines fold change and precision, and carries the direction).

```{r fgsea, echo=TRUE}
ranks <- limma_results %>% arrange(desc(t)) %>% pull(t, name = gene)

run_fgsea <- function(gene_sets) {
  set.seed(20261105)
  fgsea(pathways = gene_sets, stats = ranks, minSize = min_size, maxSize = max_size, eps = 0) %>%
    as_tibble() %>% arrange(padj)
}

gsea_hallmark <- run_fgsea(hallmark)
```

```{r plot-gsea, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
gsea_hallmark %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  slice_max(abs(NES), n = 25, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(pretty_name(pathway), NES),
         direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up in tumor", "Down in tumor")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = NES, y = label, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Up in tumor` = "#e74c3c", `Down in tumor` = "#2980b9")) +
  labs(x = "Normalized enrichment score (NES)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "fgsea: the 25 strongest significant Hallmark sets") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The classic GSEA plot for the strongest set in each direction: the green curve is the running enrichment score, each tick one gene of the set at its rank (left = most up in the tumor). The **leading edge** is the part of the list before the peak: the genes that drive the enrichment.

```{r plot-enrichment, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
top_up_set   <- gsea_hallmark %>% filter(NES > 0) %>% slice_min(padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(pathway)
top_down_set <- gsea_hallmark %>% filter(NES < 0) %>% slice_min(padj, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(pathway)

for (set in c(top_up_set, top_down_set)) {
  print(plotEnrichment(hallmark[[set]], ranks) +
          labs(title = set, x = "Gene rank (up in tumor → down in tumor)", y = "Running enrichment score"))
}
```

# Part 5 — Do camera and GSEA Agree?

```{r agreement, echo=TRUE}
agreement <- camera_results %>%
  transmute(pathway, camera_score = -log10(PValue) * if_else(Direction == "Up", 1, -1)) %>%
  inner_join(gsea_hallmark %>% select(pathway, NES), by = "pathway")
agreement_r <- round(cor(agreement$NES, agreement$camera_score), 2)
```

```{r plot-agreement, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5}
agreement %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = NES, y = camera_score)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(color = "#8e44ad", size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "fgsea NES", y = "camera signed -log10(p)",
       title = paste0("Each point is a Hallmark set (correlation r = ", agreement_r, ")")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

<div class="alert-info">
**Broad agreement, different confidence.** Both methods rank the sets similarly (r = `r agreement_r`): same direction, same top sets. camera is usually more conservative, because it accounts for the correlation between genes; GSEA's permutations of *genes* (as in fgsea) do not. When a set is significant by both, the result is robust.
</div>

# Part 6 — GO Biological Process: Collapsing Redundancy

GO terms give more specific labels, at the cost of heavy redundancy ("cell cycle", "mitotic cell cycle", "cell cycle process"...). `collapsePathways()` keeps only the **independent** signals among the top terms.

```{r go, echo=TRUE}
gsea_go <- run_fgsea(go_bp)

top_go    <- gsea_go %>% filter(padj < 0.05) %>% slice_min(padj, n = 100, with_ties = FALSE)
# collapsePathways() works on fgsea's own data.table output, not on a tibble.
collapsed <- collapsePathways(data.table::as.data.table(top_go), pathways = go_bp, stats = ranks)
main_go   <- top_go %>% filter(pathway %in% collapsed$mainPathways)
```

```{r plot-go, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
main_go %>%
  group_by(NES > 0) %>%
  slice_min(padj, n = 12, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(label = fct_reorder(str_trunc(pretty_name(pathway), 60), NES),
         direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up in tumor", "Down in tumor")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = NES, y = label, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Up in tumor` = "#e74c3c", `Down in tumor` = "#2980b9")) +
  labs(x = "NES", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = paste0("Main independent GO BP terms (", nrow(main_go), " of the top ", nrow(top_go), " after collapsing)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r table-results}
datatable(
  bind_rows(
    camera_results %>% transmute(method = "camera", collection = "Hallmark", pathway, direction = Direction,
                                 FDR = signif(FDR, 3), NES = NA_real_),
    gsea_hallmark %>% transmute(method = "fgsea", collection = "Hallmark", pathway,
                                direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up", "Down"), FDR = signif(padj, 3), NES = round(NES, 2)),
    main_go %>% transmute(method = "fgsea", collection = "GO BP (main terms)", pathway,
                          direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up", "Down"), FDR = signif(padj, 3), NES = round(NES, 2))
  ) %>% filter(FDR < 0.05) %>% arrange(collection, method, FDR),
  extensions = "Buttons",
  options = list(dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("csv", "excel"), pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE),
  rownames = FALSE,
  caption = "Every significant result (FDR < 0.05)."
)
```

```{r export, echo=TRUE}
write_csv(camera_results, "results/camera_hallmark.csv")
bind_rows(Hallmark = gsea_hallmark, `GO BP` = gsea_go, .id = "collection") %>%
  mutate(leadingEdge = map_chr(leadingEdge, ~ paste(.x, collapse = ";"))) %>%
  write_csv("results/fgsea_results.csv")
```

# Part 7 — Reading the Results With Care

- **Up in tumor: proliferation.** Cell-cycle programs (`E2F_TARGETS`, `G2M_CHECKPOINT`, `MYC_TARGETS`) dominate: Wilms tumor is made of dividing embryonic-like cells, while mature kidney cells rarely divide.
- **Down in tumor: what the tumor lacks.** Immune and inflammatory programs (`INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE`, `TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB`, `INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE`), coagulation and mature metabolic functions describe **which cells are missing** from a tumor sample (resident immune and stromal cells, mature tubule cells) rather than a pathway switched off inside tumor cells. Bulk RNA-seq always mixes cell types.
- **Competitive tests depend on the background.** "Up" means "more up than the typical gene in this comparison".
- **An enriched set is a hypothesis.** It tells us that the genes of a program move together, not why. The leading-edge genes (in `results/fgsea_results.csv`) are where to look next.

# Summary

- **camera** (limma) is a competitive test that corrects for **inter-gene correlation**, working directly on expression and the paired design.
- **GSEA** (fgsea) ranks all genes by the moderated t-statistic and needs no cutoff.
- Using both, and **collapsing** redundant GO terms, gives a robust, readable picture of the biology behind the DEG list.
